steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Installation transforms a whole space — the viewer physically enters the artwork, becoming part of the experience.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mixed media combines different materials and processes in one piece — breaking down boundaries between art forms.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Found objects (ready-mades) bring existing meaning and context — Duchamp's Fountain challenged what counts as art.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Site-specific work responds to a particular location — its architecture, history, atmosphere or community.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring installation and mixed media. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with installation and mixed media. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with installation and mixed media. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to installation and mixed media, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined out | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
